findings.summary: C++17 PUBLIC interface requirement silently dropped — all four libraries set target_compile_features(PUBLIC cxx_std_17) in CMake but no equivalent cxxopts or toolchain feature is present in any Bazel cc_library target
findings.evidence: cmake side: internal_utils.cmake:198 calls `target_compile_features(${name} PUBLIC cxx_std_17)` for every library created by cxx_library_with_type, making C++17 a PUBLIC (transitive) requirement for consumers. Bazel side: elements/googletest/googletest/BUILD.bazel and elements/googletest/googlemock/BUILD.bazel carry no `cxxopts = ["-std=c++17"]`, no `features = ["c++17"]`, and no Bazel toolchain constraint — the standard is not propagated to consumers.

findings.summary: pthreads link library missing despite GTEST_HAS_PTHREAD=1 being baked in — Bazel targets define the macro but omit -lpthread from linkopts
findings.evidence: cmake side: internal_utils.cmake:194-196 calls `target_link_libraries(${name} PUBLIC Threads::Threads)` whenever GTEST_HAS_PTHREAD is set (which it is on Linux). Bazel side: all four cc_library targets in googletest/BUILD.bazel and googlemock/BUILD.bazel carry `defines = ["GTEST_HAS_PTHREAD=1"]` but have no `linkopts = ["-lpthread"]` or equivalent threading dep. Binaries that link these targets and exercise thread-using code paths will fail at link time with undefined references to pthread symbols.

findings.summary: SYSTEM include-path property lost — gtest/gmock headers become project includes for consumers instead of system includes, breaking -Werror builds
findings.evidence: cmake side: googletest/CMakeLists.txt:144-148 uses `target_include_directories(gtest SYSTEM INTERFACE ...)` and `target_include_directories(gtest_main SYSTEM INTERFACE ...)` (SYSTEM suppresses warnings in consumer translation units). googlemock/CMakeLists.txt:106-111 does the same for gmock and gmock_main. Bazel side: elements/googletest/googletest/include/BUILD.bazel and elements/googletest/googlemock/include/BUILD.bazel use `includes = ["."]`, which generates -I flags (not -isystem). Consumers with -Werror will receive warnings from gtest/gmock headers as if they were project headers.

findings.summary: GTestConfig.cmake and GTestConfigVersion.cmake absent from install bundle — find_package(GTest CONFIG) consumers will fail
findings.evidence: cmake side: googletest/CMakeLists.txt:91-106 generates GTestConfigVersion.cmake via write_basic_package_version_file and GTestConfig.cmake via configure_package_config_file, then installs both to lib/cmake/GTest/. These are the entry-point files required for config-mode find_package. Bazel side: elements/googletest/BUILD.bazel only generates lib/cmake/GTest/GTestTargets.cmake (via gen_lib_cmake_GTest_GTestTargets_cmake write_file). GTestConfig.cmake and GTestConfigVersion.cmake are not generated anywhere, so an external CMake project calling find_package(GTest CONFIG) against this install tree will silently fail at configure time.

findings.summary: CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF not carried into Bazel copts — GNU C++ extensions may be active where CMake required strict ISO C++
findings.evidence: cmake side: CMakeLists.txt:10 sets `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF` for non-Cygwin/MSYS/QNX platforms, which instructs the compiler to use -std=c++17 rather than -std=gnu++17 (disabling GNU extensions). Bazel side: no `-fno-gnu-extensions` or equivalent copt is present in any of the four cc_library targets. Depending on the Bazel toolchain default, GNU extensions may be enabled, differing from the CMake intent.
